the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Base change to a perfect closure k inside k': the restrictions R_i' to R_i are universal homeomorphisms as compositions of base changes of the universal homeomorphism U' to U (see the diagram in the restrict-groupoid-on-field lemma), so it suffices to prove the closedness of a'(R_1') in R_2'; assume k perfect. For perfect k the closure of the image is a groupoid scheme Z inside R_2 by the map-groupoids-on-perfect-field-image lemma, and the same lemma applied to id_{R_1} : R_1 to R_1 shows (R_2)_red is a groupoid scheme. Applying the open-image-is-closed lemma to the morphism a restricted to (R_2)_red, viewed as a morphism (R_2)_red to Z, gives that the image is closed in Z; it is also dense in Z by definition of Z as the closure, hence equals Z, so a(R_1) = Z is closed in R_2. (source lines 1822-1845)
